component.name: Moonglow Toolset
component.summary: Build modules for Neverwinter Nights: Enhanced Edition

description.p: Moonglow is a module toolset for Neverwinter Nights: Enhanced Edition, a reimplementation of BioWare's Aurora Toolset that runs on Linux, Windows and macOS. It edits what Aurora edits: areas with their tiles and objects, blueprints and palettes, conversations, journals, factions, scripts and module properties, and builds, verifies and tests the module in the game.
Moonglow reads the game's data from your installation; it needs a copy of Neverwinter Nights: Enhanced Edition.

Files out of the toolset: To Scratch in the script editor (the script compiled, with its compiled script) and the area view copies loose files into a folder of your choice, such as a server's development folder; Export as Files and Copy to Scratch Folder in the module tree; mg export --files from the command line.

Plugins (experimental): commands and checks of your own, written in Luau and run in a sandbox, installed from a file and off until enabled; their edits are one step of Undo, and their checks run with Verify Module. The plugin API is at 0.1 and may still change. The Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) finds any command, and every menu command can be given a key. Compile All Scripts, Build Module and Verify Module run in the background, with progress and Cancel. mg set and mg apply change a module's fields from the command line.

Several areas' properties are edited together: Edit Areas Together lists the module's areas to tick, by name, tileset and kind, and sets their lighting, fog, weather, music, scripts and variables at once; mg areas does the same from the command line. Variables edited for several objects merge into each. Forms have ruled headings, and labels in the regular face.

Merchants and sounds are hidden by what stands in front of them: they were drawn over the view. Merchants stay yellow arrows, or the game's $ sign (Options, Area); sounds are the game's markers for them. The Variables window's name field shows a whole name.

Waypoints show the flags of their appearance; the area view draws the ranges of placed sounds, lights a dark area evenly with its lighting switched off, and moves its camera up and down (Z and C, or Ctrl + Shift with the wheel or a middle drag); areas can be listed by name rather than ResRef; the Options window keeps its size; and the cliffs of the Forest - Facelift tileset are drawn whole.

Areas on custom tilesets whose door counts are no counts (values left by the editor that wrote them) open again: Moonglow froze on them, its memory growing. A tileset with a group missing loads; Area Properties reads the tileset once, not on every frame.

An armor's parts take colors of their own (the game's per-part colors, which Aurora has no page for), edited on the item's Appearance page and shown in previews; the Eraser drags as terrain brushes do; a body part whose model names a missing texture is drawn with its own.

Painting terrain shows the tiles a click or a drag will make before it is made; drags fill a rectangle or follow its outline with Shift and let go of what they pass when run back; a Refine Tile tool steps a tile through those that fit. Blueprints show where they will be placed and turn with Q and E; merchants preview what they sell; tabs rename what they show; and the editors use the whole window, with bold labels.

JSON output from every command-line tool, and mg find and mg info for questions about a module; NWSync publishing (Build › Publish to NWSync… and mg nwsync), as nwn_nwsync_write publishes; a tileset editor that changes only the lines it edits, makes the tileset's palette and renders its minimap pictures.

Palettes find blueprints by tag and close matches, show a picture on hover, and keep favorites and recent ones; a talk-table editor and 2DAs shown with their text and the hak each row comes from; a hak editor, and haks and a talk table attached to a module in one step; placeable and door walkmeshes in the area view, and minimaps exported as the game draws them; keys that can be changed in Options.

Modules as nasher projects for git; Find References and Rename everywhere; Verify names what crashes Aurora in custom content; Test From Here and reloading changed haks; placement tools and prefabs; go to definition, references, renaming and live errors in scripts, and an NWScript language server; fields for EE data Aurora hides; bulk edits and Find and Replace; conversations that play as the game plays them and go out to and come back from text, CSV, Twine and Ink.

Editors open in windows over the area view; blueprints drag from the palette into areas; previews follow their editors and show placed objects; the camera turns with a right drag and moves with W, A, S and D; layout and usability fixes throughout.
First release: functional parity with the Aurora Toolset.
